title: Tenant Oasis: reservation profiles & fallback handbook
content:
Background:

This is a working PRD for a new take on dedicated pool management: Tenant Oasis. Objective is to provide predictable baseline capacity for committed tenants while enabling controlled, low-friction burst above that baseline using a lightweight handshake and telemetry-driven fallback system. Unlike previous proposals that focused primarily on credit pools or slots, Oasis introduces reservation profiles and cushion bands to better reflect burst patterns, isolation needs, and contractual SLAs.

High level goals (what success looks like):
- Customers have a clear, predictable baseline (reservation) + a defined burst envelope with transparent behavior.
- Product exposes simple primitives: reservationProfile, cushionBand, burstHandshake.
- Platform maintains per-tenant SLO attainment >= 99.9% for baseline traffic and graceful degradation for burst events.
- Operator tooling to visualize oasis states, spillbacks, and per-tenant ripple-backpressure.

Primary users:
- Platform/product teams (configure tiers, contracts)
- SRE/operators (runbooks, alerts)
- Customer infra/eng (understand contract and fallback behavior)

Scope (in):
- Reservation profiles: baseline vCPU/GPU slots, memory/KV cache allocations, and token quotas.
- Cushion bands: soft additional capacity buckets sized to workload profiles (percent of baseline).
- Burst Handshake Protocol (BHP): ephemeral token issuance with TTL to allow short-term burst above cushion; includes verification and automated revoke when capacity constrained.
- Soft preemption semantics: graceful throttling and automatic model-variant fallback when preemption occurs.
- Console panels and simple API to inspect tenant oasis state and active handshakes.

Out of scope (for this draft):
- Full marketplace-style exchange of burst credits between tenants.
- Pricing/rate card changes (billing team will provide once models are defined).

Key concepts (new wording intentionally):
- Reservation Profile: static reservation (guaranteed) + metadata (priority, allowed model classes, warm pools).
- Cushion Band: a soft headroom envelope expressed as percentage of baseline and max TTL for handshakes. Not guaranteed.
- Burst Handshake: a 3-step ephemeral token flow where tenant requests handshake, platform provisionally issues token referencing cushion band, then verifies backend capacity and confirms/denies. Tokens support pushback hints for client-side degrade.
- Safety Fence: hard isolation boundary; no burst tokens cross this fence. Typically used for high-compliance tenants or noisy-neighbor protection.
- Ripple Backpressure: gradual reduction in handshake acceptance across related tenants to avoid global collapse — spreads the pain rather than a single hot-tenant causing systemic failure.

Design (sketch):
1) Reservation profile data model (API-facing):
- id: string
- baseline_capacity: numeric (vGPU-equivalent units)
- allowed_model_tags: list
- priority_tier: low|standard|high
- warm_pool: boolean
- cushion_band_pct: numeric (e.g., 30)
- cushion_ttl_seconds: numeric
- safety_fence: boolean

2) Burst Handshake Protocol (BHP):
- Step A: POST /tenants/{id}/handshake {requested_pct, preferred_ttl}
- Step B: Platform returns provisional token + estimated confirmation latency (optimistic).
- Step C: Platform confirms token within TTL or returns deny; client receives degrade_hint in deny response.

Client behavior expectations (brief):
- Use handshake for short synchronous bursts (spike QPS, longer prompt contexts).
- Respect deny/degrade hints: fallback to cheaper model, reduce prompt length, use cached embeddings.

Isolation controls and safety fences:
- Safety fences are binary: if set, tenant cannot exceed baseline. This is exposed in tenant profile and enforced at admission.
- For standard tenants we rely on cushion bands + ripple backpressure.
- Operators can configure cross-tenant attenuation curves: when cluster free capacity falls below X%, handshake acceptance decays per-tenant weight.

Autoscaling interaction:
- Oasis integrates with predictive autoscaler:** autoscaler consumes handshake telemetry as an early spike signal.
- Two autoscale modes: baseline-autoscale (slow, conservative) and cushion-reactive (fast, limited by policy).
- If cushion usage sustained > cushion_profile.allowed_duration, trigger baseline expansion proposal (billing/ops flow).

Telemetry and observability (console):
- Per-tenant metrics: baseline_utilization, cushion_utilization, handshake_rate, handshake_accept_ratio, denied_tokens, safety_fence_triggers.
- Cluster metrics: global_free_capacity_pct, ripple_backpressure_index, handshake_confirmation_latency_p50/p95.
- Alerts: sustained cushion_utilization > 70% for 5m -> notify capacity ops + send tenant owner email.
- Dashboard: tenant oasis panel showing current cushion consumption, active handshakes, and degradation hints.

Runbook (operator-facing):
- If ripple_backpressure_index > 0.7: escalate to SRE (page) + temporarily increase attenuation thresholds for low-priority tenants.
- If handshake_confirmation_latency_p95 > 2s: check scheduler queue and warm_pool health.
- Preemption flow: platform sends preemption webhook to tenant endpoint with suggested degrade strategy.

APIs and UX notes (short):
- Expose GET /tenants/{id}/oasis -> returns reservationProfile + current state.
- UI: small status chip next to tenant name (green=y baseline ok, amber=cushion in use, red=fence active/denied).
- Onboarding flow: when creating reservation, show recommended cushionBand based on observed historical QPS distribution (auto-suggest).

Billing and contract implications (notes for finance):
- Cushion should be free for short bursts up to X minutes/day; beyond that convert to billable overage or recommend baseline upsell.
- Need to define smoothing window and convert sustained cushion usage to auto-propose baseline increase.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal alpha): implement reservationProfile + internal-only BHP with manual operator confirmation.
- Phase 1 (beta): automated BHP w/ default attenuation curves, UI panel, tenant opt-in.
- Phase 2 (GA): configurable cushion bands in console, safety fence toggle, billing hooks + SLA language.

Migration story (existing tenants):
- Default: create reservationProfile with baseline equals current observed 30-day 95th percentile usage; cushionBand default 20%.
- Provide one-click toggle in console to opt into Oasis or remain on legacy quota.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to price cushion without disincentivizing usage? (finance + GTM)
- Exact attenuation curve math and whether to weight by recent error budgets (SRE)
- Interaction with model-aware autoscaler: when a tenant uses high-capacity models during burst, do we throttle model class or block handshake?
- Security: handshake tokens must be HMAC-signed with short TTL — who manages keys? (security)
- Need simple simulator to model ripple backpressure across 100 tenants.

Action items:
- Product: flesh out API contract + example payloads (Ben)
- Applied ML/Serving: run quick sim to estimate cushion effectiveness across typical enterprise burst shapes (Marco)
- SRE: propose attenuation defaults and runbook entries (Eve)
- Finance: draft potential overage pricing and baseline-upgrade triggers (Priya)

Notes / references:
- Related tickets: JIRA-DDC-987 (traffic shaping), JIRA-DDC-1003 (warm pool health).
- Proto PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/412 — early handshake prototype.

Rough timeline: 8 weeks to Beta if we prioritize core token flow and console panels. Alpha can be done in 3 weeks with operator-only issuance.

Short-term experiment idea:
- Pick 10 medium tenants; enable cushionBand 25% for 2 weeks; measure error rates, baseline SLO violations, and cost delta. If cushion reduces latency stalls with <10% infra cost increase, expand to more tenants.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the naming intentionally human-friendly (oasis, cushion) so sales can explain it.
- Avoid market-sounding "burst credits" until finance ok's the word.
- Make sure console UX surfaces "degrade_hint" clearly in realtime logs so devs can react.

End of draft.
